newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 a tonne higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 a tonne higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $5 higher Wednesday as traders expect the market to get a boost from currency-linked buying.

Strength in the British pound against the dollar overnight could prompt arbitrage to focus on buying cheaper dollar-denominated New York cocoa, they said. The dollar softened after the Fed decided to leave key U.S. interest rates unchanged Tuesday.

London cocoa futures were broadly lower early Wednesday, pressured by sterling's strength. LIFFE July cocoa was down nine stg at the midday break at 1,015 stg, with Sepember slipping the same to 1,034 stg.

Tuesday, New York cocoa futures ended broadly lower in slim dealings, pressured by a late-session round of local liquidation. July ended down $8 at $1,469 a tonne after trading between $1,483 and $1,467. Second-month September closed $9 lower at $1,495, while the back months sagged $6.

Technically, trader said the July contract would need to get above $1,490, where buy-stops are thought to be building, in order to fill a key chart gap between $1,494 and $1,501. July support was pegged at $1,465, followed by $1,450-$1,446.
